docs.title: License & Attribution
docs.text:
PandaWare uses a dual license: one license for documentation and hardware designs, another for firmware/source code.

Content type License Documentation (this site) & hardware designs (CAD, STL, STEP, schematics) CC BY 4.0 Firmware & other source code MIT

docs.title: Using PandaWare's designs or docs
docs.text:
You're free to share and adapt them, including commercially, as long as you give credit. Suggested attribution text:

Based on PandaWare (https://github.com/ShreyaSutar-engi/pandaware), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

Full terms: LICENSE-DOCS.md

docs.title: Using PandaWare's firmware
docs.text:
The firmware is MIT licensed — do effectively anything with it, including in closed-source or commercial projects, as long as you keep the copyright notice.

Full terms: LICENSE

docs.title: Hero media
docs.text:
Drop your hero image or video here (e.g. hero.jpg, hero.mp4, or an animated GIF of the hand gripping something).

Then in docs/index.md, replace the .pw-hero__media placeholder <div> with an <img> or <video> tag pointing at this file, e.g.:

<img src="assets/hero/hero.jpg" alt="PandaWare prosthetic hand" class="pw-hero__media-img">

or for video:

<video class="pw-hero__media-img" autoplay muted loop playsinline>
  <source src="assets/hero/hero.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

This file itself (favicon.svg) is a placeholder icon — swap it for a real PandaWare logo whenever you have one, keeping the filename the same (or update theme.favicon in mkdocs.yml if you rename it).
